title: Berlin Water Hardness - Quick Summary
items: **All Berlin tap water is officially hard.** The nine waterworks delivered 15,1 to 23,3 German degrees (°dH) as their 2025 annual medians, and every one of the 190 Berlin postcodes sits in the hard class, grade hart (3).

**Your postcode has its own official range.** Berliner Wasserbetriebe publishes per-postcode values: around Wedding the network runs about 14,0 to 15,7 °dH, while parts of the east and southeast reach 18,6 to 25,7 °dH. The same kettle scales at different speeds across town.

**The crust in your kettle is calcium carbonate.** Carbonate hardness, roughly 9 to 16 °dH depending on the postcode, is the part that turns into scale when water is heated. It is a mineral deposit, not dirt and not a pollutant.

**Set your machines to your postcode, not to a guess.** Dishwasher: set the hardness to the upper end of your range and keep regenerating salt topped up. Washing machine: dose from the hard column on the detergent pack. Kettle and coffee machine: descale with citric acid on a regular rhythm.

**The water is safe to drink everywhere.** Hardness is calcium and magnesium from Berlin's own groundwater, controlled under the German drinking water ordinance. You do not need a filter for safety; an espresso machine is the one appliance where a filter genuinely earns its money.
